annotations-on Capability: custom annotations stamped on every object (ON) FAIL
Description
Renders the product chart with a global annotation knob set (extraAnnotations.example\.com/owner=team-x) and asserts every rendered object (all kinds) carries the configured annotation at .metadata.annotations. ---
id: annotations-on
name: "Capability: custom annotations stamped on every object (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a global annotation knob set (extraAnnotations.example\.com/owner=team-x) and asserts every rendered object (all kinds) carries the configured annotation at .metadata.annotations. The sample chart does NOT expose an extraAnnotations/commonAnnotations knob — this scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks global annotation propagation.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: true
    "extraAnnotations.example\\.com/owner": team-x
asserts:
  - type: annotations-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    annotations:
      example.com/owner: team-x
tags: [capability, compliance, curated-live]
category: capability
capability: annotate-all-objects
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:annotations"]

---
id: gateway-api-istio-gateway-api-basic
name: "Istio Gateway API Basic"
description: "Installs istio/base + istio/istiod and Gateway API CRDs, creates GatewayClass istio + Gateway + HTTPRoute, and verifies HTTP routing through auto-provisioned Istio data-plane."
labels: {customer: any, profile: gateway-api}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api/releases/download/v1.2.0/standard-install.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    gatewayRoute.enabled: "true"
    gatewayRoute.parentRef.name: "sample-gw"
    gatewayRoute.parentRef.sectionName: "http"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-gateway-api-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'gateway-api:istio']
category: gateway-api
integration: istio
tier: live

      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},

---
id: ingress-controllers-contour-basic-httpproxy
name: "Contour basic HTTPProxy (gap-probe)"
description: >-
  Installs Contour, creates an HTTPProxy for the product Service via fixture, and verifies HTTP routing through the envoy pod IP with Host header matching and HTTPProxy status valid. Then runs a gap-probe: the chart does NOT natively emit a Contour HTTPProxy CRD — the HTTPProxy was created by the fixture, not by a chart template. This is an honest gap (red cell); do NOT over-engineer the chart.
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: projectcontour/contour
      version: "0.6.0"
      release: contour
      namespace: projectcontour
      repo:
        name: projectcontour
        url: "https://projectcontour.github.io/helm-charts"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/contour-basic-httpproxy.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: projectcontour
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/contour-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:contour']
category: networking
integration: contour
tier: live

---
id: labels-on
name: "Capability: extra labels stamped on every object (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with a global extra-label knob set (extraLabels.team=platform, extraLabels.cost-center=42) and asserts every rendered object (all kinds, not just pod templates) carries the configured labels at .metadata.labels. The sample chart does NOT expose an extraLabels/commonLabels knob — this scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks global label propagation.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: true
    extraLabels.team: platform
    extraLabels.cost-center: "42"
asserts:
  - type: labels-present
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    labels:
      team: platform
      cost-center: "42"
tags: [capability, compliance, curated-live]
category: capability
capability: label-all-objects
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:labels"]

Installs Kong Ingress Controller, deploys the product chart with ingress.enabled=true and ingress.className=kong, and verifies end-to-end routing through the Kong proxy data path via the chart's built-in Ingress resource. Also includes a KongPlugin gap-probe documenting that the sample chart exposes no konghq.com/plugins annotation or KongPlugin CRD knob, which is an honest gap (red cell) — do NOT over-engineer the chart.

---
id: networking-kong-ingress
name: "Kong Ingress (className=kong)"
description: >-
  Installs Kong Ingress Controller, deploys the product chart with ingress.enabled=true and ingress.className=kong, and verifies end-to-end routing through the Kong proxy data path via the chart's built-in Ingress resource. Also includes a KongPlugin gap-probe documenting that the sample chart exposes no konghq.com/plugins annotation or KongPlugin CRD knob, which is an honest gap (red cell) — do NOT over-engineer the chart.
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: kong/ingress
      version: 0.24.0
      release: kong
      namespace: kong
      repo:
        name: kong
        url: "https://charts.konghq.com"
      values:
        ingressController:
          enabled: true
          ingressClass: kong
          installCRDs: true
        proxy:
          type: NodePort
          http:
            enabled: true
            nodePort: 30080
          tls:
            enabled: true
            nodePort: 30443
        env:
          database: "off"
        replicaCount: 1
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "true"
    ingress.className: "kong"
    ingress.host: "sample.test.local"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: kong
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/kong-ingress.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:kong']
category: networking
integration: kong
tier: live

---
id: networking-metallb-loadbalancer
name: "MetalLB LoadBalancer (service.type=LoadBalancer)"
description: >-
  Installs MetalLB, configures an IPAddressPool + L2Advertisement whose CIDR is inside the kind Docker bridge subnet, deploys the product chart with service.type=LoadBalancer, and verifies that MetalLB assigns an external IP from the pool and the LB endpoint serves HTTP 200.
labels: {customer: any, profile: loadbalancer}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: metallb/metallb
      version: 0.16.1
      release: metallb
      namespace: metallb
      repo:
        name: metallb
        url: "https://metallb.github.io/metallb"
      values:
        controller:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "50m"
              memory: "64Mi"
        speaker:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "50m"
              memory: "64Mi"
        installCRDs: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/metallb-ip-pool.yaml
      namespace: metallb
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    service.type: "LoadBalancer"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: metallb
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/metallb-loadbalancer.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:metallb']
category: networking
integration: metallb
tier: live

scenario.yaml 1809 B · 69 ln

---
id: networking-traefik-ingress
name: "Traefik Ingress (className=traefik)"
description: >-
  Installs Traefik, deploys the product chart with ingress.enabled=true and ingress.className=traefik, and verifies end-to-end routing through the Traefik data path via the chart's built-in Ingress resource.
labels: {customer: any, profile: ingress}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: traefik/traefik
      version: v28.3.0
      release: traefik
      namespace: traefik
      repo:
        name: traefik
        url: "https://traefik.github.io/charts"
      values:
        image:
          registry: ghcr.io
          repository: traefik/traefik
        ingressClass:
          enabled: true
          isDefaultClass: false
        ingressRoute:
          dashboard:
            enabled: false
        ports:
          web:
            exposedPort: 80
          websecure:
            exposedPort: 443
        service:
          type: NodePort
        providers:
          kubernetesIngress:
            enabled: true
          kubernetesCRD:
            enabled: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "true"
    ingress.className: "traefik"
    ingress.host: "sample.test.local"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: traefik
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/traefik-ingress.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:traefik']
category: networking
integration: traefik
tier: live

scenario.yaml 2715 B · 81 ln

---
id: policy-opa-gatekeeper-required-labels
name: "OPA Gatekeeper required labels enforcement (gap-probe)"
description: >-
  Installs OPA Gatekeeper + NGINX Ingress, creates k8srequiredlabels ConstraintTemplate + Constraint targeting Deployments and Ingresses. Verifies non-compliant resources denied, compliant accepted. Cross-feature compose with M4 nginx-ingress. Then runs a gap-probe: the chart's Ingress template uses selectorLabels (just app: <release>) instead of the full common labels (which include app.kubernetes.io/name), so the chart's Ingress fails the required-labels constraint — an honest gap (red cell); do NOT over-engineer the chart.
labels: {customer: any, profile: policy}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: gatekeeper/gatekeeper
      version: "3.17.1"
      release: gatekeeper
      namespace: gatekeeper-system
      repo:
        name: gatekeeper
        url: "https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts"
      values:
        auditInterval: 10
        constraintViolationsLimit: 20
        enableExternalData: false
        postInstall:
          labelNamespace:
            enabled: false
        validatingWebhookFailurePolicy: Fail
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 4m
    - kind: helm
      chart: ingress-nginx/ingress-nginx
      version: "4.10.0"
      release: ingress-nginx
      namespace: ingress-nginx
      repo:
        name: ingress-nginx
        url: "https://kubernetes.github.io/ingress-nginx"
      values:
        controller:
          service:
            type: NodePort
          allowSnippetAnnotations: true
          ingressClassResource:
            name: nginx
            enabled: true
            default: false
            controllerValue: "k8s.io/ingress-nginx"
          watchIngressWithoutClass: true
        admissionWebhooks:
          enabled: false
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/k8srequiredlabels-template.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    image.repository: "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx"
    image.tag: "1.27-alpine"
    ingress.enabled: "false"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: gatekeeper-system
    timeout: 4m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: ingress-nginx
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/opa-gatekeeper-required-labels.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:opa-gatekeeper', 'addon:nginx-ingress']
category: policy
integration: opa-gatekeeper
tier: live

---
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredlabels
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredLabels
      validation:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            labels:
              type: array
              items:
                type: string
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8srequiredlabels
        violation[{"msg": msg, "details": {"missing_labels": missing}}] {
          provided := {label | input.review.object.metadata.labels[label]}
          required := {label | label := input.parameters.labels[_]}
          missing := required - provided
          count(missing) > 0
          msg := sprintf("Missing required label(s): %v", [missing])
        }

Renders the product chart with rbac.create=true and serviceAccount.create=true and asserts a ServiceAccount, Role or ClusterRole, and matching RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding are present with correct wiring (roleRef, subjects, serviceAccountName). The sample chart does NOT include RBAC templates — no serviceaccount.yaml, role.yaml, or rolebinding.yaml exists. Setting rbac.create=true has no effect because the chart lacks the templates. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks rbac.create and serviceAccount.create knobs.

---
id: rbac-on
name: "Capability: RBAC objects present when enabled (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with rbac.create=true and serviceAccount.create=true and asserts a ServiceAccount, Role or ClusterRole, and matching RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding are present with correct wiring (roleRef, subjects, serviceAccountName). The sample chart does NOT include RBAC templates — no serviceaccount.yaml, role.yaml, or rolebinding.yaml exists. Setting rbac.create=true has no effect because the chart lacks the templates. This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks rbac.create and serviceAccount.create knobs.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    rbac.create: true
    serviceAccount.create: true
asserts:
  - type: rbac-objects
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    expect_present: true
tags: [capability, compliance, curated-live]
category: capability
capability: rbac-toggle
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:rbac"]

scheme-https-only Capability: HTTPS-only scheme enforcement (ON) FAIL
Description
Renders the product chart with TLS enabled (tls.enabled=true) and asserts no plain-HTTP Service port, container port, probe, or Ingress backend is present. The sample chart does NOT support suppressing the HTTP port — when TLS is enabled it merely ADDS an HTTPS port (443) alongside the always-present HTTP port 80 on the Service, containerPort 80 on the Deployment, probes targeting port 80, and the Ingress backend pointing at service.port (80). This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks an HTTPS-only / http-disable knob. A TLS secret fixture is preinstalled so the chart can deploy with tls.enabled=true.

---
id: scheme-https-only
name: "Capability: HTTPS-only scheme enforcement (ON)"
description: >-
  Renders the product chart with TLS enabled (tls.enabled=true) and asserts no plain-HTTP Service port, container port, probe, or Ingress backend is present. The sample chart does NOT support suppressing the HTTP port — when TLS is enabled it merely ADDS an HTTPS port (443) alongside the always-present HTTP port 80 on the Service, containerPort 80 on the Deployment, probes targeting port 80, and the Ingress backend pointing at service.port (80). This scenario is EXPECTED to FAIL (honest red gap) documenting that the chart lacks an HTTPS-only / http-disable knob. A TLS secret fixture is preinstalled so the chart can deploy with tls.enabled=true.
labels: {customer: enterprise, profile: compliance}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/manual-tls-basic-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: true
    tls.secretName: manual-tls-basic
    ingress.enabled: true
    ingress.host: sample.local
asserts:
  - type: scheme-enforced
    namespace: sample
    source: rendered
    scheme: https-only
tags: [capability, compliance, curated-live]
category: capability
capability: protocol-scheme
tier: capability
mechanisms: ["capability:scheme"]

      mountPath: "",

      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",

      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},

    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

service-mesh-istio-ambient-live Istio Ambient Mesh — Live mTLS Verification (ztunnel/HBONE) PASS
Description
Installs istio/base + istio/istiod (profile=ambient) + istio/cni (profile=ambient) + istio/ztunnel, annotates the product namespace istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=false (NO sidecar), and proves: (1) ztunnel DaemonSet pods are Ready in istio-system, (2) the product namespace carries the ambient annotation and every product pod has exactly 1 container (no istio-proxy), (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS over HBONE — confirmed via ztunnel metrics/logs. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 1-container pod manifest, ambient-annotated namespace manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: false, and versions.json.

kind

---
id: service-mesh-istio-ambient-live
name: "Istio Ambient Mesh — Live mTLS Verification (ztunnel/HBONE)"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod (profile=ambient) + istio/cni (profile=ambient) + istio/ztunnel, annotates the product namespace istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=false (NO sidecar), and proves: (1) ztunnel DaemonSet pods are Ready in istio-system, (2) the product namespace carries the ambient annotation and every product pod has exactly 1 container (no istio-proxy), (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS over HBONE — confirmed via ztunnel metrics/logs. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 1-container pod manifest, ambient-annotated namespace manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: false, and versions.json.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        profile: ambient
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/cni
      version: 1.27.9

---
id: service-mesh-istio-ingress-gateway-basic
name: "Istio Ingress Gateway — Basic"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod + istio/gateway, deploys the product chart with ingress disabled, creates an Istio Gateway + VirtualService to route external traffic through the ingressgateway pod, and verifies HTTP 200 via the gateway with a Host header.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/gateway
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-ingressgateway
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        service:
          type: NodePort
          ports:
            - name: http2
              port: 80
              nodePort: 30080
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    ingress.enabled: false
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-ingressgateway
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istio-ingressgateway
    timeout: 3m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 3m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-ingress-gateway-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-ingress-gateway']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio
tier: live

Description
Installs istio/base + istio/istiod, enables mesh injection, deploys the product chart with scope.enabled=true, creates a PeerAuthentication with mode=STRICT in the product namespace, and verifies: (a) plain HTTP from a non-mesh pod is rejected, (b) in-mesh probe pod still reaches the product Service with 200 via auto-upgraded mTLS.

scenario.yaml 1925 B · 67 ln

---
id: service-mesh-istio-service-mesh-strict-mtls
name: "Istio Service Mesh — strict mTLS"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod, enables mesh injection, deploys the product chart with scope.enabled=true, creates a PeerAuthentication with mode=STRICT in the product namespace, and verifies: (a) plain HTTP from a non-mesh pod is rejected, (b) in-mesh probe pod still reaches the product Service with 200 via auto-upgraded mTLS.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    mesh.inject: "true"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-strict-mtls.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-service-mesh']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio
tier: live

helm_values:
  {replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {type: ClusterIP, port: 80}, tls: {enabled: false, secretName: "", servicePort: 443,
      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",
      # -- Whether to run the wait-for-tls initContainer that polls for cert files. Disable for CSI volumes that are populated asynchronously.
      waitForCerts: true},
    # -- Scope component (API server). Creates a separate Deployment + Service on port 8080.
    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},
    # -- Darkroom component (async processor). Creates a separate Deployment with optional PVC mount.
    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},
    # -- Ingress resource for skywatcher Service.

    # -- HTTPRoute resource for Gateway API integration.
    gatewayRoute: {enabled: false, parentRef: {name: envoy, namespace: "", sectionName: ""}, hostname: ""},

service-mesh-istio-sidecar-live Istio Sidecar Mesh — Live mTLS Verification PASS
Description
Installs istio/base + istio/istiod, pre-labels the product namespace istio-injection=enabled via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=true, and proves: (1) istiod is Ready and the sidecar injector webhook is present, (2) every product pod has exactly 2 containers including istio-proxy, (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS — confirmed via istio-proxy stats reporting non-zero inbound SSL handshakes. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 2-container pod manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: true, and versions.json.

---
id: service-mesh-istio-sidecar-live
name: "Istio Sidecar Mesh — Live mTLS Verification"
description: >-
  Installs istio/base + istio/istiod, pre-labels the product namespace istio-injection=enabled via raw_manifest, deploys the chart with mesh.inject=true, and proves: (1) istiod is Ready and the sidecar injector webhook is present, (2) every product pod has exactly 2 containers including istio-proxy, (3) in-mesh traffic to the product Service returns HTTP 200 and the connection is mTLS — confirmed via istio-proxy stats reporting non-zero inbound SSL handshakes. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with 2-container pod manifest, applied-overrides recording inject: true, and versions.json.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/base
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istio-base
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    - kind: helm
      chart: istio/istiod
      version: 1.27.9
      release: istiod
      namespace: istio-system
      repo:
        name: istio
        url: "https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts"
      values:
        pilot:
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: "100m"
              memory: "384Mi"
        global:
          proxy:
            holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 5m
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/istio-inject-namespace.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    mesh.inject: "true"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istio-base
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: istiod
    namespace: istio-system
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: istio-system
    selector: app=istiod
    timeout: 5m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/istio-sidecar-live.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:istio', 'mesh:istio-sidecar']
category: service-mesh
integration: istio
tier: live

---
id: service-mesh-linkerd-live
name: "Linkerd — Live mTLS Sidecar Mesh"
description: >-
  Installs linkerd-crds + linkerd-control-plane (with a preinstalled trust anchor / issuer cert via raw_manifest), annotates the product namespace with linkerd.io/inject=enabled, deploys the chart, and proves: (1) linkerd control-plane pods Ready and proxy-injector webhook present, (2) every product pod has a linkerd-proxy container alongside the app container, (3) linkerd check --proxy -n sample exits 0 confirming the data plane is healthy. Emits a PASS artifact bundle with a 2-container pod manifest, linkerd.io/inject-annotated namespace, and versions.json.
labels: {customer: any, profile: mesh}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    # Step 1: Install Linkerd CRDs (required before control-plane)
    - kind: helm
      chart: linkerd/linkerd-crds
      version: 1.8.0
      release: linkerd-crds
      namespace: linkerd
      repo:
        name: linkerd
        url: "https://helm.linkerd.io/stable"
      values: {}
      wait: helm-deployed
      wait_timeout: 2m
    # Step 2: Pre-create linkerd namespace + identity issuer Secret (trust anchor via raw_manifest)
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/linkerd-identity-secret.yaml
    # Step 3: Install Linkerd control plane with REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME cert placeholders.
    # linkerd-live.sh generates real ephemeral certs and upgrades the release before
    # any other checks run, so the initial install uses wait:none (pods won't be Ready
    # with placeholder certs).
    - kind: helm
      chart: linkerd/linkerd-control-plane
      version: 1.16.11
      release: linkerd-control-plane
      namespace: linkerd
      repo:
        name: linkerd
        url: "https://helm.linkerd.io/stable"
      values: ./fixtures/linkerd-live-values.yaml
      wait: none
    # Step 4: Annotate the product namespace for linkerd injection (before product chart install)
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/linkerd-inject-namespace.yaml
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set: {}
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: linkerd-crds
    namespace: linkerd
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: linkerd-control-plane
    namespace: linkerd
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/linkerd-live.sh
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: linkerd
    timeout: 10m
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:linkerd', 'mesh:linkerd']
category: service-mesh
integration: linkerd
tier: live

---
# Linkerd control-plane values for live scenario.
# The trust anchor ConfigMap is pre-created via raw_manifest (linkerd-identity-secret.yaml),
# so externalCA=true tells the chart to skip creating it.
# The issuer cert/key are provided here (required by the chart) to create the Secret.
# REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME markers are substituted with ephemeral ECDSA P-256 certs
# by the linkerd-live.sh assertion script — DO NOT add real private key material.
proxy:
  resources:
    cpu:
      limit: "250m"
      request: "100m"
    memory:
      limit: "256Mi"
      request: "64Mi"
identity:
  externalCA: true
  issuer:
    scheme: linkerd.io/tls
    tls:
      crtPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME
      keyPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME
identityTrustAnchorsPEM: REPLACE_AT_RUNTIME

---
id: tls-cert-manager-self-signed
name: "cert-manager self-signed Issuer -> CA Cert -> CA Issuer -> leaf Cert"
description: >-
  Installs cert-manager with CRDs, applies a self-signed Issuer, a CA Certificate bootstrapping a CA Secret, a CA Issuer backed by that Secret, and a leaf Certificate for the product Service FQDN. Deploys chart with tls.enabled=true and tls.secretName pointing at the issued Secret. Verifies HTTPS 200 with --cacert and SAN match.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: helm
      chart: jetstack/cert-manager
      version: v1.14.0
      release: cert-manager
      namespace: cert-manager
      repo:
        name: jetstack
        url: "https://charts.jetstack.io"
      values:
        installCRDs: true
      wait: pods-ready
      wait_timeout: 3m
    # Chain: self-signed Issuer -> CA Certificate -> CA Issuer -> leaf Certificate
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/selfsigned-issuer.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/ca-certificate.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/ca-issuer.yaml
      namespace: sample
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/leaf-certificate.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: sample-tls
    tls.servicePort: "443"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/tls-cert-manager-self-signed.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:cert-manager']
category: certificates
integration: cert-manager
tier: live

The chart mounts it with tls.volumeType=secret (default) and serves HTTPS 200. Validates Secret type, data keys, PEM validity, and in-cluster HTTPS reachability.

---
id: tls-manual-secret
name: "Manual TLS Secret via raw_manifest"
description: >-
  Delivers a pre-provisioned kubernetes.io/tls Secret (RSA 2048) via raw_manifest preinstall sourced from chart-test/fixtures/, no inline base64 blobs. The chart mounts it with tls.volumeType=secret (default) and serves HTTPS 200. Validates Secret type, data keys, PEM validity, and in-cluster HTTPS reachability.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/manual-tls-basic-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: manual-tls-basic
    tls.servicePort: "443"
    tls.volumeType: "secret"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/manual-tls-basic.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:manual-tls-secret']
category: certificates
integration: manual-tls-secret
tier: live

      # -- Filesystem path where TLS cert+key are mounted. Defaults to /etc/tls.
      mountPath: "",
      # -- Volume type for the TLS material. Supported: secret (default), persistentVolumeClaim, projected, csi.
      volumeType: "secret",
      # -- PVC claim name (required when volumeType is persistentVolumeClaim).
      pvcClaimName: "",
      # -- SecretProviderClass name (required when volumeType is csi).
      secretProviderClass: "",

      waitForCerts: true},

    scope: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, service: {port: 8080}},

    darkroom: {enabled: false, replicaCount: 1, image: {repository: nginx, tag: "1.27-alpine"}, pvc: {enabled: false, claimName: "", mountPath: /data}},

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    default.conf: |
      server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }
      server {
        listen 443 ssl;
        server_name _;
        ssl_certificate     /etc/tls/tls.crt;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/tls/tls.key;
        location / {
          root /usr/share/nginx/html;
          index index.html;
        }
      }

tls-mounted-projected TLS via projected volume PASS
Description
Creates a kubernetes.io/tls Secret, then deploys the chart with tls.volumeType=projected so the pod has a projected volume sourcing the TLS Secret. Verifies projected volume source, tls.crt/tls.key present at mountPath, and in-cluster HTTPS curl returns 200.

scenario.yaml 1106 B · 36 ln
View full file 
---
id: tls-mounted-projected
name: "TLS via projected volume"
description: >-
  Creates a kubernetes.io/tls Secret, then deploys the chart with tls.volumeType=projected so the pod has a projected volume sourcing the TLS Secret. Verifies projected volume source, tls.crt/tls.key present at mountPath, and in-cluster HTTPS curl returns 200.
labels: {customer: any, profile: tls}
cluster:
  provider: kind
  k8s_version: v1.30.0
  preinstall:
    - kind: raw_manifest
      path: ./fixtures/mounted-tls-projected-secret.yaml
      namespace: sample
product:
  chart: ./chart
  release: sample
  namespace: sample
  set:
    tls.enabled: "true"
    tls.secretName: mounted-tls-projected
    tls.servicePort: "443"
    tls.volumeType: "projected"
asserts:
  - type: helm-status-deployed
    release: sample
    namespace: sample
  - type: pods-ready
    namespace: sample
    timeout: 5m
  - type: smoke-script
    path: chart-test/assertions/mounted-tls-projected-volume.sh
tags: [nightly, curated-live]
mechanisms: ['addon:mounted-tls-certs']
category: certificates
integration: mounted-tls-certs
tier: live
